changes.after: Represent a value that may be missing without confusing missing with zero.

before: std::optional<int> holds either an int or no value. std::nullopt constructs the empty state; it does not mean the integer zero.

In if(result), optional converts to true when a value is present, even when that value is 0. Only dereference *result after establishing presence; dereferencing an empty optional is not a safe fallback.
Expected output or behavior: value 0. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Return an optional position from a search and handle both found-at-zero and not-found cases. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: std::optional<int> holds either an integer or no value. std::nullopt means no value is present. Zero is still a real integer value, so it is different from missing.
if (result) checks whether the optional contains a value. It does not test whether the contained integer is nonzero. has_value() asks the same presence question directly.
*result reads the contained value. First establish that a value is present. An empty optional must not be dereferenced as if it contained a default integer.
The program prints value 0. reward(true) returns an optional containing zero, so the presence check succeeds.
value_or supplies a fallback when an optional is empty. It returns a value without filling the optional. Use a fallback only when treating absence that way makes sense for the task.

before.question: Change reward(true) to reward(false). Which branch runs, and why?
choices: missing: there is no contained int.
value 1: optional converts the payload to a bool first.
value 0: absence and zero are the same.
before.explanation: false selects nullopt. The condition checks presence, not the numeric truthiness of an int.

after.question: Change reward(true) to reward(false). Which branch runs?
choices: missing, because no integer is contained.
value 1, because the contained value is converted to true.
value 0, because missing and zero mean the same thing.
after.explanation: false makes reward return nullopt. The optional is empty, so the presence check chooses the missing branch.
